note: Ps54 'Save me by your name' (corrected; Ziphite betrayal). A plea psalm - God-action heavy. Human IB core: the prayer (tefillah), the endangered then God-upheld nefesh (life/soul, x2), the enemies' ruthlessness (arits) + life-seeking + evil, and the resolving freewill (nedabah) thanksgiving + triumphant looking. God-qualifiers=14 (save/name/vindicate/might/hear/give-ear anchored to the prayer; helper/upholder to the nefesh; return/faithfulness/end/name/good/delivered to evil/thanks). Re-roled: freewill-offering + looked (human acts) qual->char; helper char->qual; strangers/risen/enemies/sacrifice/trouble/hiding -> standalone. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: aloud, the words of his mouth
appealing to God's name and might to save and vindicate (v1)

'O God, hear my PRAYER (tefillah); give ear to the words of my mouth' — the whole psalm's engine: the endangered man casting himself on God in prayer; tefillah the appeal that leans on God's name and might (v1, the qualifiers) to save and vindicate — trust voiced as petition
ruthless / violent men (arits - ruthless men seek my life)
they do not set God before themselves
paired with seeking the psalmist's life

'RUTHLESS men (arits) seek my life; they do not set God before themselves' — the violent, God-ignoring aggressors; arits (the ruthless/terror-inspiring) the enemies whose godlessness (like the fool, Ps53) frees them to hunt the psalmist's life without restraint
the murderous intent of the ruthless men
'ruthless men SEEK (baqash) my life' — the deadly pursuit; baqash here the hunting of the psalmist's nefesh — the enemies' settled aim to take his life, the threat the prayer answers

'ruthless men seek my LIFE (nefesh)' — the psalmist's very life, the contested centre; nefesh (life/soul) here what the enemies hunt — the same nefesh that God is said to uphold (v4), the self endangered and then sustained
life / soul (nefesh - upholder of my life)
God the helper and upholder of this life (v4)

'the Lord is the upholder of my LIFE (nefesh)' — the endangered soul now sustained; nefesh here the life the enemies sought (v3), held up by God the helper (the qualifiers) — the turn from threat to confident security, 'Behold, God is my helper'
evil / harm (ra - return the evil to my enemies)
God will return it upon the enemies (v5)

'He will return the EVIL (ra) to my enemies' — the enemies' own malice boomeranged; ra here the harm they devised, which God (the qualifier, 'he will return') turns back on their own heads — poetic justice, the evil recoiling on its authors
freewill / voluntary offering (nedabah - with a freewill offering)
paired with giving thanks to God's name

'With a FREEWILL OFFERING (nedabah) I will sacrifice to you' — the willing, spontaneous devotion of the rescued; nedabah (voluntary/freewill, cf the willing spirit nadib Ps51:12) the gladness of a heart that gives not from duty but overflow — worship offered freely, twinned with thanksgiving
give thanks / praise (yadah - give thanks to your name)
because God has delivered him from every trouble (v7) in his faithfulness (v5)

'I will GIVE THANKS (yadah) to your name, O LORD, for it is good' — the grateful response to deliverance; yadah here thanksgiving to God's good name (the qualifier), the answer of the rescued heart, offered freely because God has delivered him from every trouble (v7)
look (in triumph) (raah - my eye has looked on my enemies)
because God put an end to the enemies (v5)

'my eye has LOOKED (raah) in triumph on my enemies' — the vindicated gaze of the delivered; raah here the psalmist's own eye beholding the downfall of those who sought his life — not gloating cruelty but the settled assurance of God's justice done (cf the righteous laughing, Ps52:6)
save (yasha - save me by your name)
God's saving invoked in the prayer (v1)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'SAVE (yasha) me, O God, by your name' - God's saving is not a human IB char; the deliverance the psalmist's prayer (279975) appeals for, 'by your name'. Qualifier.
God's name, the power the prayer leans on (v1)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's name): 'save me by your NAME (shem)' - God's revealed name/character is not a human IB char; the divine power the prayer (279975) invokes for rescue. Qualifier.
vindicate / judge (din - vindicate me by your might)
God's vindicating invoked in the prayer (v1)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'VINDICATE (din) me by your might' - God's judging/vindicating is not a human IB char; the just verdict the prayer (279975) asks, 'by your might'. Qualifier.
God's might, the power the prayer leans on (v1)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's might): 'vindicate me by your MIGHT (gevurah)' - God's power is not a human IB char; the strength the prayer (279975) appeals to for vindication. Qualifier.
God's hearing asked of the prayer (v2)
v2 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'O God, HEAR (shama) my prayer' - God's hearing is not a human IB char; the attention the psalmist's prayer (279975) seeks. Qualifier.
give ear (azan - give ear to the words of my mouth)
God's attending asked of the prayer (v2)
v2 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'GIVE EAR (azan) to the words of my mouth' - God's attending is not a human IB char; twin of 'hear', the listening the prayer (279975) begs. Qualifier.
God the helper who sustains the psalmist's life (v4)

v4 QUALIFIER (God's role): 'Behold, God is my HELPER (azar)' - God's helping is not a human IB char (re-roled from an earlier mis-call); the divine aid that upholds the psalmist's nefesh (279998). Qualifier.
uphold / sustain (samak - upholder of my life)
God who upholds the psalmist's nefesh (v4)
v4 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'the Lord is the UPHOLDER (samak) of my life' - God's sustaining is not a human IB char; the divine upholding that secures the endangered nefesh (279998). Qualifier.
God returns the enemies' evil upon them (v5)
v5 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'He will RETURN (shub) the evil to my enemies' - God's requital is not a human IB char; the divine act that turns the enemies' own evil (280000) back on them. Qualifier.
God's faithfulness, ground of the thanksgiving (v5->v6)

v5 QUALIFIER (God's faithfulness): 'in your FAITHFULNESS (emet) put an end to them' - God's reliability is not a human IB char; the divine constancy on which the psalmist rests his plea for judgment and his thanks (280009). Qualifier.
put an end / destroy (tsamath - put an end to them)
God ends the enemies, so the psalmist looks on them in triumph (v5->v7)

v5 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'put an END (tsamath) to them' - God's destroying of the enemies is not a human IB char; the judgment that lets the psalmist look on his enemies vindicated (280020). Qualifier.
name (shem - give thanks to your name)
God's name, the object of the thanksgiving (v6)
v6 QUALIFIER (God's name): 'I will give thanks to your NAME (shem)' - God's name is not a human IB char; the object toward which the psalmist's thanksgiving (280009) is directed. Qualifier.
the goodness of God's name, ground of the thanks (v6)

v6 QUALIFIER (God's goodness): 'for it (your name) is GOOD (tob)' - the goodness of God's name is not a human IB char; the divine quality that grounds the thanksgiving (280009), 'for it is good' (cf Ps52:9). Qualifier.
deliver / rescue (natsal - he has delivered me)
God's deliverance from every trouble, ground of the thanks (v7->v6)

v7 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'For he has DELIVERED (natsal) me from every trouble' - God's rescue is not a human IB char; the deliverance that grounds the freewill thanksgiving (280009) and the triumphant looking. Qualifier.
hide oneself (sathar - Is not David hiding among us)

superscription (historical heading): 'when the Ziphites... told Saul, Is not David HIDING (sathar) among us?' - David's outward concealment/flight that occasions the psalm; narrative framing in the heading, an external act, not the psalm's inner-being content. Standalone.

v3: 'STRANGERS (zur) have risen against me' - the alien/insolent enemies as persons (the Ziphites/aggressors); the ruthlessness they embody is read in 279984 - here the bare identification of the enemy. Standalone.
rise up (qum - have risen against me)

v3: 'strangers have RISEN (qum) against me' - the enemies' outward act of rising up in hostility; the aggression itself, its inner malice carried in the ruthless-men char (279984). Standalone (hostile act).
enemies / watchful foes (shorer - to my enemies)
v5: 'He will return the evil to my ENEMIES (shorer)' - the foes as persons, the target of God's requital; their evil is the char (280000), here the bare naming of those judged. Standalone.
sacrifice (zabach - I will sacrifice to you)

v6: 'With a freewill offering I will SACRIFICE (zabach) to you' - the outward cultic act of offering; the inner willingness is the char (nedabah, 280007) and the gratitude is give-thanks (280009) - here the ritual act itself. Standalone (cultic act).
trouble / distress (tsarah - delivered from every trouble)

v7: 'he has delivered me from every TROUBLE (tsarah)' - the affliction/distress the psalmist is rescued from; the outward straits (the enemies' assault), the object of God's deliverance (280015), not itself an inner operation. Standalone.
